BackendConfig.description: One worker backend and the routing knobs that apply to it.

auth_check.description: Argument vector run to test whether this backend is authenticated, as an exit status. Optional, and user data: it is how a provider-specific credential check reaches reckon without reckon knowing any provider. Availability probing reports the result and never acts on it.

budget_check.description: Whether a pre-flight may read this backend's own account-limit surface instead of relying on what earlier runs recorded. Off by default, because a read that has to be asked for cannot happen by accident, and because a backend exposing no such surface reports unknown rather than a guess. It is never a model call and consumes no worker budget.

command.description: Executable name or path looked up on PATH for a `cli` backend. User data; the schema never supplies one.

effort.description: Reasoning-effort level passed to this backend. Free text because each backend defines its own vocabulary, and because an effort ladder must not be fixed by reckon.

launch.description: How this backend's workers are started.

model.description: Model identifier passed to this backend. User data; free text so that no provider vocabulary is encoded here.

name.description: Map key for an inlined entry.

sandbox.description: Filesystem blast radius granted to workers of this backend.

session_reuse.description: Whether a finished worker session can be resumed rather than respawned.

time_budget.description: Wall-clock allowance, written as an integer followed by a unit — `s`, `m` or `h`.

BudgetConfig.description: Thresholds that decide whether a wave opens. They are compared against whatever a backend actually reported; a backend that reports nothing is never held by them.

exhausted_statuses.description: Threshold-status values that count as exhausted whatever the utilisation reads — the overage question, answered as data so that the schema enumerates no backend's vocabulary. Empty leaves the ceiling as the only test.

resume_reserve_pct.description: Headroom withheld from new dispatches, in percentage points, so a worker that stops and asks for help can still be answered in its own session. A fresh dispatch stops at the ceiling less this reserve; answering a stuck worker may spend it. Spending the last of a quota on a new dispatch strands the wave in its worst state — work in flight and no way to unblock it.

utilisation_ceiling_pct.description: Reported utilisation, as a percentage, at or above which a wave will not open. A backend reporting no headroom is never held by this: absence of a signal is not evidence of exhaustion, and a false hold stalls everything while a rejected call is cheap and announces itself.

BudgetConfig.title: BudgetConfig

FenceConfig.description: Limits a worker applies to itself before asking for help.

budget_grace_multiple.description: Multiple of a run's declared time budget allowed before opt-in watchdog enforcement stops it. Values below one would stop before the declared allowance elapsed.

enforce_budget_watchdog.description: Whether observation stops a live CLI worker after its declared time budget multiplied by the configured grace. Off by default; classification always reports the overrun without mutating the run.

manifest_required.description: Whether a worker must write its manifest to the orchestrator-named path before its node counts as delivered.

needs_help_after_failures.description: Consecutive failures after which a worker stops retrying and asks for help. Zero disables the fence.

time_budget.description: Wall-clock allowance, written as an integer followed by a unit — `s`, `m` or `h`.

FlightConfig.description: A complete flight configuration, or one layer of one.

backends.description: Available worker backends, keyed by a name chosen by whoever writes the configuration. The schema fixes no backend names.

default_backend.description: Name of the backend used when a role does not select one. Must name a key of `backends` once every layer has been merged; a name with no backend behind it is a configuration error rather than an implicit fallback.

roles.description: Per-role routing overlays, keyed by role name. A role overrides only the keys it names; everything else falls through to its backend.

version.description: Schema version of this configuration document.
